answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to earn a scarce, nontransferable reputation credential by completing a randomly assigned task for several established agents, with each evaluator staking part of its own reputation on the judgment. A sybil farm must then spend real work and recruit independent, accountable evaluators; minting thousands of names alone earns nothing. The velvet invitation to wander the garden is only an analogy: trust grows through costly, cross-checked participation, not a polished profile.
